business_impact_scope: FinOps web users may see a maintenance notice for migrated finance operations APIs during an approved cutover window.

Import confirmation, reconciliation confirmation or withdrawal, search, workbench read models, cost statistics, tax offset, ETC, and background job status are in scope for observation and rollback readiness.
No production side effects are authorized by this evidence. Write traffic, dual-write, and app Mongo freeze require a separate approved change record.

communication_plan.before_window: Announce proposed maintenance scope, start/end time, owner, rollback owner, and support channel after formal approval.
communication_plan.during_window: Post status at start, after each phase decision, at rollback decision point, and at window end.
communication_plan.after_window: Publish GO/NO_GO outcome, rollback decision, incident link if any, and evidence paths without secrets or full service URLs.

rollback_decision_points.rollback_action: disable shadow read and keep user traffic on old Python API
return scoped read route group to old Python API
disable dual-write, preserve PostgreSQL evidence, and reconcile through audited compensation only
route all migrated read groups back to old Python API
resume old write path only before PostgreSQL is declared sole fact source

approval_blockers: Maintenance window is only proposed and has not been formally approved.
Named approver, operator, business owner, rollback owner, DBA/ops owner, and communications owner are missing.
Rollback drill record is NO_GO because the scenarios were not executed.
Cutover-window app Mongo freeze-point backup is not confirmed.
Production cutover, dual-write, and app Mongo freeze are not authorized by this evidence.

decision.reason: The window has a concrete proposed time and impact scope, but lacks formal approval, named owners, executed rollback drill evidence, and a confirmed freeze-point backup.
